description: Panel power switch - drives the load switch enable, carries no load current
package: PANEL MOUNT, wired: M6x0.75 bushing, solder-lug terminals (code 01) both lugs wired to the main board, beside U-LOADSW - nothing on the jack board connects to it
notes: Signal-level only - it sits in the top leg of the LT1641's ON divider (R-ON-HI/R-ON-LO) and carries about 0.15 mA, no load current. The only power switch in the system; SW-PWR-INST is deleted (ADR 0005). *** CONTACT MATERIAL G, GOLD - NEVER W. *** 0.15 mA is still two orders of magnitude below a silver contact's wetting current, so silver oxidises and goes intermittent after months - a reliability fault that passes every bench test. NKK's own catalogue example is M2012SS1W01, silver; do not copy it. M2011 is a true SPST ('M2011 model does not have terminal 1' - the M2012 SPDT with one throw omitted). D4 (D-FLAT) OVER S4 (KEYWAY): both need a non-round hole, but a 5.8mm D-flat can be filed by hand where a keyway needs a broach or a mill, and this is a one-off panel. THE PANEL HOLE IS THE TRACKED FIGURE panel-toggle-hole; do not restate it. MOUNT IT THROWING LEFT-RIGHT, ON TO THE RIGHT (ADR 0024 point 12): the panel's D-flat is on the LEFT, because the M2011 is ON with its lever away from the flat [ds NKK-SERIES-M-TOGGLE.pdf p.5 and p.7], and its lugs then lie in a row across the panel. config/module.yaml layout.toggle_on owns the side. The D4 hardware is two hex nuts and a lockwasher, no locking ring [ds p.7]: the flat is the only anti-rotation feature. FIT ONE NUT, ON THE FRONT, with the lockwasher; the second nut is NOT fitted behind the panel. The body seats flat against the panel's rear face, as the module CAD models it (mechanical/cad/module.scad, 'nut SW-POWER'); a rear nut would move the body and its lugs back by config/module.yaml toggle.nut_h toward the main board, into the room the lugs' wires bend in. Bushing thread 8.9mm against a 2mm panel leaves 6.9mm for the nut and washer; max panel thickness with the standard hardware is 2.6mm, so it fits with 0.6mm to spare. Body 7.9mm across, 9.4mm deep behind the bushing; toggle 10.5 x 2.8mm dia, 25 deg throw; solder lugs at 4.7mm pitch. M2RE/M6RE in the Multicomp sheet are TERMINAL style codes, not an M6 thread code - do not misread them. WIRED, NOT PCB-MOUNTED: terminal code 01 is a solder lug [ds NKK-SERIES-M-TOGGLE.pdf p.4], and the body is deeper behind the bushing than the gap to the jack board (ADR 0023), so it is wired, not board-mounted: column 5 says where its wires land

description: Current-limited hot-swap controller on the umbilical +12V feed
source: DigiKey (or Newark, ADI direct) - not LCSC
notes: Current-limited hot-swap controller on the umbilical +12V feed. Its two companions are separate rows: the pass FET is Q-LOADSW and the sense resistor is R-ILIM. SUFFIX MATTERS: the -1 LATCHES OFF and is restored only by interrupting power or pulsing ON low; the -2 auto-retries at a 3.75% duty cycle into a persistent short. PINOUT: 1 ON, 2 FB, 3 PWRGD, 4 GND, 5 TIMER, 6 GATE, 7 SENSE, 8 VCC. *** FB, PIN 2, MUST BE DIVIDED DOWN FROM THE OUTPUT - NEVER LEFT OPEN. *** Foldback keys off V_FB, not off V_OUT ('the current folds back as a function of the output voltage, which is sensed at the FB pin', p.8), so with FB at 0V the limit sits at 12mV/50mohm = 240mA permanently, the output never charges, the timer ramps forever and the -1 latches. That is 'the instrument never starts', and no C-TIMER value fixes it; R-FB-HI/R-FB-LO are what set it. From the banked 164112fc.pdf: VCC UVLO 7.5 / 8.3 / 8.8 V, which holds GATE low regardless of ON; I_GATE -5 / -10 / -20 uA [p.2]; I_TIMER pull-up -24 / -80 / -132 uA [p.2]; the 12mV-to-47mV-at-VFB=0.5V law [Figure 7, p.9]. Package S8, theta-JA 110 degC/W. I GRADE, -40 to +85 degC [164112fc p.2 order table]: the C grade's 0 degC floor is the one a rack in a van in winter breaks. IN PRODUCTION: ADI lists LT1641-1IS8#PBF as PRODUCTION, and its one PCN, 24_0246, moves the marking to the top side [web https://web.archive.org/web/20260412125011/https://www.analog.com/en/products/lt1641-1.html, ADI's page as captured 2026-04-12; analog.com is unreachable from here]. HAND-PLACED AND BOUGHT FROM A DISTRIBUTOR: LCSC/JLC hold none (C664552, 0). On 2026-10-03 DigiKey had 253 at $9.38, factory lead 20 weeks [web https://www.digikey.com/en/products/result?keywords=LT1641-1IS8%23PBF]; Newark 272, ADI direct 51 [web https://www.findchips.com/search/LT1641-1IS8%23PBF]. Buy 2-3 with the first module order.

description: Pass FET for U-LOADSW, on the umbilical +12V feed
notes: Nexperia's hot-swap part: 'Enhanced forward biased safe operating area for superior linear mode operation', applications 'Electronic fuse, Hot swap, Load switch, Soft start' [ds NEXPERIA-PSMN2R0-30YLE.pdf p.1]. CHOSEN ON THE SINGLE-PULSE SOA AT V_DS = 12 V, which is what decides this part - not R_DS(on). What it must survive and the margin it has are in umbilical-load-switch.md, 'What sizes the FET'; not restated here. 30 V, VGS +/-20 V: GATE rises up to 18 V above VCC, so D-GATE-CLAMP is not optional. Logic level (3.5 mohm max at VGS 4.5 V), which the LT1641 requires below 20 V of supply [164112fc p.10]. Pins 1-3 S, 4 G, mounting base D [p.2]: the drain is the tab, so the tab's copper is the SENSE_NODE. LCSC C553247, 1379 in stock at $1.16 [web LCSC 2026-09-30]

description: HF decoupling at every module IC supply pin
notes: One per supply pin, close to the pin, each netted on its circuit's sheet as C-DEC-*: 7 x OPA2197 on +/-12V = 14 (U-RESP's two included - it is on the sheet, proposed, and if E10 drops it this count falls by two), INA828 = 2, DAC8568 AVDD = 1 (its only supply pin), 74AHCT125 VCC, 74AHCT14 VCC (C-DEC-RX), LT1641 VCC, LT3042 in (U-REG-DAC, C-DEC-REG-IN). Count from the parts on the sheets, not from this number

description: Sets the load switch current limit
notes: THE resistor that is the limit, and the limit has a spread whatever it is: V_SENSETRIP is 39 / 47 / 55 mV [164112fc p.2], so 50 mohm gives 0.78 / 0.94 / 1.10 A, and the foldback floor (8 / 12 / 17 mV) 160 / 240 / 340 mA. FIXED AT 50 MOHM, NOT SELECTED ON THE BENCH: the whole spread passes - at the low corner of both thresholds and of the timer the hot-plug start still finishes inside the fault time (umbilical-load-switch.md, 'What the start actually takes'). E6 still measures the trip with a current probe, as a check. Metal plate, +/-50 ppm/C, 1 W [ds RALEC-LR1206-CURRENT-SENSE.pdf p.3]; 1.1 A dissipates 61 mW in it. KELVIN-CONNECT SENSE and VCC to its pads [164112fc p.10]. LCSC C154645, 2855 in stock [web LCSC 2026-09-30]

description: Upper leg of the LT1641 FB divider, umbilical +12V to FB
notes: The FB divider. Its values and their derivation are the tracked figure loadswitch-fb-divider, owned by umbilical-load-switch.md and not restated here; what follows is what a reader of THIS row needs. FB must be divided down from the output at all - see U-LOADSW for why an open FB latches the part off. *** V_FB = 0.5V AND THE PWRGD THRESHOLD V_FBH = 1.313V ARE SET BY THE SAME DIVIDER, *** so V_OUT(full 47mV limit) = 0.381 x V_OUT(PWRGD) ALWAYS - 'cross 0.5V early in the ramp' and 'PWRGD means the output is good' are ONE decision, not two, and the ratio is fixed by the part, not by these resistors. It is therefore sized at the PWRGD end, which is the end with a hard requirement: PWRGD must release below the worst-case delivered output of ~11.36V (Eurorack +12V at -5%, less the sense and FET drops). The foldback law behind it, verbatim [p.5, drawn as Figure 7 p.9]: 'The current limit circuit will regulate the voltage across the sense resistor (VCC - VSENSE) to 47mV when VFB is 0.5V or higher. If VFB drops below 0.5V, the voltage across the sense resistor decreases linearly and stops at 12mV when VFB is 0V.' Divider current is 294uA at 12V, 294x the 1uA max FB input current [p.2], so leakage is <=0.34% of the ratio

description: Lower leg of the LT1641 FB divider, FB to PWR_GND
notes: Partner to R-FB-HI. Same blocker: the divider ratio follows from the foldback law and the PWRGD threshold, both of which are search-index text until analog.com is reachable | 2026-09-21 VALUE SET. 5.11k against R-FB-HI's 35.7k is a ratio of 6.986 against the 7.00 the 10.5V PWRGD target wants. See R-FB-HI and power-entry.md for the derivation and the worst-case table

description: Series gate resistor between LT1641 GATE and the N-FET gate
notes: NEW 2026-09-21, read straight off ADI's typical application [164112fc Figure 5, p.8] once the datasheet was banked. It is R5 there, and the text says what it is for: 'R5 prevents high frequency oscillations in Q1' [p.7]. This page drew GATE going straight to the FET. Not a judgement call - it is the manufacturer's reference circuit for the part, and the FET it damps is the one that has to hold 940mA steady for 47ms on every hot-plug

description: Compensation resistor in series with C-GATE-LOADSW, GATE to PWR_GND
notes: NEW 2026-09-21, from ADI's typical application [164112fc Figure 5, p.8], where it is R6: 'Resistor R6 provides current control loop compensation' [p.7]. IT IS IN SERIES WITH THE GATE CAPACITOR, not in parallel with anything - the schematic here had C-GATE-LOADSW going straight to ground, which removes the compensation zero from the current-limit loop. C-GATE's ramp calculation is unaffected (the 1k sees 10uA, i.e. 10mV)

description: Top of the LT1641 ON (UVLO) divider, ISO_POS12 to the toggle
notes: With R-ON-LO it sets the undervoltage trip; the thresholds and why they sit there are in umbilical-load-switch.md, 'The ON pin'. SW-POWER is in series with it, so the toggle's wires never carry ISO_POS12 unlimited: a lug shorted to the panel pulls ON low, which is OFF. 0805W8F6802T5E, LCSC C17801

description: Bottom of the LT1641 ON divider, ON to PWR_GND
notes: Holds ON at 0 V while the toggle is open - that is OFF, and cycling the toggle is the ON pulse that restores the -1 after a latch [164112fc p.9]. 0805W8F1002T5E, LCSC C17414

description: ON pin noise filter, ON to PWR_GND at the pin
notes: The datasheet's own: 'A 0.1uF capacitor from the ON pin to GND also helps reject induced noise' [164112fc p.10] - and this node has the toggle's two wires hanging off it. With the divider's 8.7k it is a 0.87 ms time constant, which also debounces the lever. CC0805KRX7R9BB104, LCSC C49678

Cathode to the FET gate, anode to its source (UMBILICAL +12V). REQUIRED BY THE DATASHEET, NOT A PREFERENCE: 'In applications over a 9V to 24V range, a logic level N-FET must be used with a proper protection Zener diode between its gate and source (as D1 shown is Figure 5)' [164112fc p.10]. GATE is clamped at 18 V above VCC; Q-LOADSW's VGS is 20 V max, and on a shorted output the source is at 0 V. 14.25-15.75 V [ds ONSEMI-MMSZ5221BT1-SERIES-MMSZ5245BT1G.pdf]. When the part latches and pulls GATE low, the output discharges forward through it into GATE's pull-down, as in ADI's Figure 5. LCSC C129730

Fault timer capacitor for U-LOADSW. The value is the tracked figure loadswitch-timer and its derivation is in umbilical-load-switch.md; neither is restated here. TWO THINGS BIND WHEN BUYING IT. *** SPECIFY A LOW-LEAKAGE PART *** - at this value it is electrolytic or large ceramic, where leakage is a meaningful fraction of the 3 uA TIMER pull-down, and a leaky part means the timer never resets. And the package is through-hole radial or 1210 ceramic: an 0805 C0G cannot hold it. Fault time over the pull-up's own bounds is 587 / 160 / 95.6 ms, so the worst case is 95.6 ms against a 47.5 ms hot-plug start - 2.01x, which is the margin that actually had to be met. Datasheet hard minimum is 1.5 nF [p.5], not binding here

description: Gate capacitor programming the load switch ramp
notes: Programs the LT1641's output ramp: C = I_GATE / (dV/dt). The value and the ramp window it produces are the tracked figure loadswitch-gate-cap; do not restate them. THE THING TO KNOW BEFORE SIZING ANYTHING AROUND IT IS THAT I_GATE IS A 4:1 WINDOW - I_GATEUP = -5 / -10 / -20 uA [164112fc p.2], corroborated independently by the DC1354A demo quick-start guide p.1. THE ENVELOPE IS THE SPECIFICATION: ADR 0005 was widened to it on 2026-09-30 (owner: 'Good to widen the spec'), so do not size anything against a narrower ramp. BOTH CORNERS ARE SAFE: the fast corner (537mA of charging into the page's 2.2mF bound) climbs out of the 240mA foldback floor by 1.69V of output and never approaches 940mA; the slow one never enters current limit (umbilical-load-switch.md, 'The two capacitors'). C0G/NP0 or film, 50V - the dielectric matters, because a Y5V here re-programs the ramp with temperature. 1206 C0G, the same part as C-FILT-MOD: Murata GRM31C5C1H823JA01L, LCSC C97947 [ds MURATA-GRM31C5C1H823JA01L-82NF-C0G-1206.pdf]
